title: Complete Evaluator with AST: Num, Var, UnaryOp, BinOp
description: AST nodes: Num(value), Var(name), UnaryOp(op,operand), BinOp(op,left,right). evaluate uses post-order recursion: children evaluated before parent combines. Num returns value. Var looks up in env (raises NameError if missing). UnaryOp evaluates operand, returns -val for '-'. BinOp evaluates left and right, then dispatches on op (+, -, *, / with zero check, **). Test env: price=5, qty=3. Three expressions: 3+price*2=13; price*qty-1=14; -(price+1)=-6.
source: draft: omp free model + check fix: claude

steps.description: AST node classes using dataclass: Num (float value), Var (string name), UnaryOp (op, operand), BinOp (op, left, right). Tree structure encodes precedence (deeper = higher precedence).

evaluate: Num returns node.value. Var looks up in env dict, raises NameError if undefined. UnaryOp: evaluates operand, returns -val for '-'. BinOp: evaluates left then right (post-order), then matches op: +, -, *, / (zero check raises ZeroDivisionError), **. Unknown op raises ValueError.
Post-order evaluation: children evaluated completely before parent combines results. left = evaluate(node.left, env), right = evaluate(node.right, env).
Division: checks right == 0 before dividing, raises ZeroDivisionError with custom message. This is your language's error, not Python's.

steps.question: In tree = BinOp('+', Num(3), BinOp('*', Var('price'), Num(2))), which operation happens first and why?
steps.answer: The * happens first because it's the right child of +. evaluate evaluates left (3) then right (the * node). Evaluating the * node evaluates its children (price=5, 2) then multiplies -> 10. Then + adds 3+10=13. Tree structure encodes precedence.

steps.description: Test env: price=5.0, qty=3. tree1: 3 + price*2 -> 13.0. tree2: price*qty - 1 -> 14.0. tree3: -(price+1) -> -6.0 (UnaryOp wraps BinOp).
